newsitem.title: USA: Drafts restricted at key Mississippi ship channel.
newsitem.headline: Drafts restricted at key Mississippi ship channel.

text.p: The Coast Guard closed a key Mississippi River shipping channel to large vessels after a coal freighter ran aground on Tuesday, officials said.

At the mouth of the river in Southwest Pass, maritime traffic was restricted to drafts of 35 feet or less, blocking 12 southbound and four northbound vessels from navigating the channel. Normally, ships with drafts of up to 45 feet are permitted through the channel, which is located about 100 miles south of New Orleans.

Coast Guard officials said the pass was closed to all traffic immediately after the accident, but reopened to smaller vessels today. The 799-foot Chemtrans Belocean (75,000 tonne dwt) was carrying a cargo of coal at the time of the accident.
Chief Petty Officer Neal Powell, with the Coast Guard's Marine Safety Office in New Orleans, said the vessel could be refloated and the draft restrictions eased when high tide arrives in a few hours.
"Hopefully, it will be refloated then, but it's not a guarantee," he said.
The Coast Guard's Powell attributed the accident to "poor judgment on the pilot's part", though he added that the river's swift current made navigation difficult.

Heavy rains and surging floodwaters have wreaked havoc on maritime traffic on the river in recent weeks. In a separate incident today, a grain freighter bound for El Salvador collided with a docking facility near New Orleans.
While water levels on the Mississippi have finally begun to retreat, Coast Guard officials say transit on the river could remain sharply restricted for several weeks.
((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
